newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Stoiber - euro must wait if deficit high.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Stoiber - euro must wait if deficit high.

text.p: Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber said on Sunday the euro cannot be launched in 1999 in Germany if the country fails to hold its budget deficit below 3.0 percent of gross domestic product (GDP).

In an interview with the Bild am Sonntag newspaper, Stoiber said political leaders have vowed the euro would be as stable as the mark. He said Germany must stick to its promise that meeting the criteria is more important than meeting the 1999 target date.

"Even if some people say a deficit of 3.2 percent or 3.3 percent would still be acceptable, I say we cannot introduce the euro in Germany in January 1999 with these numbers," said Stoiber, who has expressed scepticism on the euro in the past.

"If we fail to reach the 3.0 percent deficit level in 1997, then our position remains that the criteria will determine the timing and not vice-versa," he added. "In other words, I prefer a delay to a weak currency."
